steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Greek drama developed from religious festivals honouring Dionysus; tragedies and comedies were performed at the City Dionysia festival in Athens

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Three great tragedians: Aeschylus (introduced second actor), Sophocles (introduced third actor, painted scenery), Euripides (questioned traditional values)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Aristophanes wrote Old Comedy that satirised contemporary politicians and issues (e.g. The Wasps, The Clouds)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Theatre was a civic institution: the state funded productions, citizens attended as a duty, and wealthy choregoi (producers) sponsored choruses as a liturgy

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: How was Greek drama connected to religion and civic life? | Q: What were the contributions of the three great tragedians? | Q: How did Aristophanes use comedy for political commentary?
